title: The Clean Deadline
premise: Xanthe Oyelaran, a disgraced intelligence analyst fired from three agencies, has spent five years living under a scrubbed identity in Lisbon, keeping a go-bag packed and a fabricated backstory polished. When a stranger named Ilya repays a favor she never performed—saving her life and demanding she honor a debt owed to 'the person you used to be'—she is dragged back into the orbit of Meridian House, the deniable training program that shaped her and then erased its own recruits. As the debt pulls her toward an assassination scheduled to coincide with the Geneva summit, Xanthe realizes the favor was engineered: Ilya is another erased recruit, and the network that trained them intends to burn its graduates as loose ends. To survive, she must assemble a found family of fellow ghosts, expose Meridian's kill-list before the summit convenes, and choose between the duty drilled into her and the love she never planned for. In the end she burns the network's archive at the cost of her own clean record, walks away with Ilya and the others, and finally unpacks the go-bag.
about_author: Gideon Ravensworth is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent a decade writing classified-adjacent briefs before turning to fiction. He lives off-grid on the Atlantic coast, where he writes about people who can't afford to be remembered.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. We meet her meticulously controlled Lisbon life: fake name, cash jobs, a go-bag by the door rehearsed down to the seconds. A routine errand goes wrong when she spots surveillance tradecraft she recognizes—Meridian House tradecraft. Emotional beat: the illusion of safety cracking; paranoia rekindled.

chapters.title: A Favor Returned
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. A stranger intercepts Xanthe at a tram stop, thanks her for saving his life in Sarajevo—a favor she never performed—and leaves a key and a warning: interest is owed. She runs her own counter-surveillance and loses him cleanly, which frightens her more than being followed. Beat: dread wrapped in curiosity.

chapters.title: The Key
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Unable to resist, she opens the deposit box: a photo of herself at twenty-two in a Meridian training facility, a partial kill-list with redacted names, and a note reading 'You were first.' Her polished lie about her past begins to rot. Beat: vertigo—the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, Three Exits
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Flashback chapter tracing how Xanthe was bounced from three agencies, each firing orchestrated by Meridian handlers keeping her isolated and deniable. Present-day Ilya watches her flat, noting she hasn't fled yet. Beat: sympathy for a woman built to be disposable.

chapters.title: Contact Protocol
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She sets a trap using dead-drop techniques she doesn't remember learning, proving her training runs deeper than her memory. Ilya takes the bait deliberately. Their first real conversation: he claims they were cohort-mates; she remembers nothing. Beat: wary alliance over shared damage.

chapters.title: What Meridian Made
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ilya explains Meridian House: a private program that recruited analysts, trained them in erasure and influence, then wiped or scattered them. The kill-list targets graduates deemed liabilities before the Geneva summit grants the network legitimacy. Beat: horror reframed as purpose—she was never paranoid, she was right.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A Meridian cleaner, Voss, makes contact posing as an old agency colleague, offering reinstatement if she delivers Ilya. Xanthe plays along while recognizing the recruitment script word-for-word. Beat: the seduction of belonging versus the taste of manipulation.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya brings Xanthe to a safehouse with two other survivors: Marisol, a forger with a wicked laugh, and Dev, a former signals man who flinches at phones. For one evening they cook dinner like ordinary people. Beat: warmth Xanthe didn't know she was starving for.

chapters.title: Memory Hole
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Under Marisol's guidance, Xanthe attempts recall exercises and recovers fragments of Sarajevo—she did save someone, but it wasn't Ilya; it was a woman whose death Meridian staged. The 'favor returned' was bait built on a buried truth. Beat: grief surfacing through amnesia.

chapters.title: The Summit Clock
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The team maps the operation: Meridian plans to eliminate eleven graduates during the summit window, framing a scapegoat to bury the program forever. They have nine days. First recon of the Geneva venue reveals security contracts run by Meridian shell companies. Beat: ticking-clock pressure hardening resolve.

chapters.title: Voss's Offer
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Voss escalates: he reveals he knows about the safehouse and offers full restoration of her record and identity in exchange for the list. For one night she genuinely considers a clean slate. Beat: love against duty begins—duty here meaning survival through obedience.

chapters.title: The Woman from Sarajevo
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Following the recovered memory, the team locates the supposedly dead woman alive in Porto: Nadia, the original savior, now hiding deeper than any of them. She confirms Meridian faked her death to test Xanthe's loyalty years ago. Beat: rage crystallizing into commitment.

chapters.title: Nine Names
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The forger reconstructs the full kill-list from fragments, discovering the eleventh name is Xanthe's—dated the day after the summit. The team realizes recruiting her was always part of the cleanup plan. Beat: betrayal inside the found family, quickly mended by Dev's quiet loyalty.

chapters.title: Counter-Surveillance
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Meridian tails them to the safehouse; a tense evasion through Porto's night market ends with Dev wounded covering their escape. Xanthe carries him out using extraction skills she hates remembering she has. Beat: the family paying blood for each other, cementing bonds.

chapters.title: Double Agent
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe walks back into Voss's net voluntarily, feeding him a false timeline while wearing a wire Dev built. Inside Meridian's front office she sees the operational board: the summit, the scapegoat, her own photograph. Beat: cold courage; the analyst fully awake again.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Nadia reveals the true prize: not the list but Meridian's archive of every recruit's file—including leverage that could expose the network's state-level patrons. Getting it means breaching the summit venue itself. The team argues over risk; Xanthe votes yes. Beat: ambition shifting from survival to justice.

chapters.title: Geneva, Day One
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Under forged credentials, the team infiltrates the summit perimeter as delegates arrive. Voss, suspicious, springs a trap meant for Ilya; Marisol is taken. Xanthe must hold her cover while her family bleeds. Beat: terror managed by discipline, love sharpening focus.

chapters.title: Exchange
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Meridian offers a trade: Marisol for the archive drive. Xanthe proposes a double-cross using the venue's own security systems against them. The exchange in a service corridor goes sideways; Voss dies by his own side's hand to protect the timeline. Beat: chaos, sacrifice, momentum.

chapters.title: Burn Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Climax. In the archive vault beneath the summit hall, Xanthe faces the program director who trained her—who reveals the final twist: the 'favor' chain began with her own recruitment file, authored by her younger self as insurance. She uploads the archive to every press desk on earth and torches the physical copies. Beat: catharsis through fire.

chapters.title: Loose Ends
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Fallout: publications begin releasing the files; summit security collapses into internal investigations; the remaining names on the list are quietly warned and scattered to safety. The found family regroups in a hospital corridor, bruised but whole. Beat: exhausted relief, the war won quietly.

chapters.title: Interest Paid
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Nadia and Xanthe finally speak plainly about Sarajevo—grief acknowledged, debt dissolved. Nadia declines to join them, choosing her own invisibility, but leaves Xanthe the truth she'd earned. Beat: closure between mirrors of the same wound.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Months later, in a new city with no alias required, Xanthe unpacks the go-bag item by item—each object a chapter of the old life—and puts it in a closet. Ilya makes coffee; Marisol sends postcards; Dev calls too often. Beat: peace chosen, memory kept, love stayed.
